ai.description: *Uropeltis liura* is a small, cylindrical snake reaching 25 cm. It is dark brown with a yellow-spotted belly and a characteristic obliquely truncated, keeled tail shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis liura* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct supraorbital ridge and the presence of a single, small, undivided rostral scale that does not split the nasals.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis liura* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis liura* is a fossorial specialist that spends most of its life underground, emerging to the surface primarily at night or after heavy rainfall.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis liura* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis liura* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation forests above 1,200 meters.
